messages:
maria_support: Heads-up — ACME (enterprise acct) opened an escalation. They say data that should be on a custom 365d retention is being queued for deletion and our Delete API is returning 500 when they try to trigger a manual removal. Customer wants an immediate pause on deletions + audit log export.

jake_eng: Can you paste the minimal repro (curl + payload + response)? Also need retention_policy_id and sample object id.

maria_support: From customer:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/objects/delete \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXX' \
  -d '{"object_id":"obj_0a1b2c3d","retention_policy_id":"rp_365_acme"}'
```
Response: 500 Internal Server Error
```
{"error":"internal_error","message":"delete failed: upstream worker error"}
```
They say policy rp_365_acme was configured in Console 2025-08-18 and shows TTL=365. Default account retention is 90. They attached screenshot.

samir_security: Do not pause anything without legal/POA from the customer. We can prepare the export and provide guidance, but legal hold requires their signed request. I can draft the export checklist.

maria_support: Got it. Customer already sent an email to compliance@acme.com with cc to our support alias — they said legal signed doc is en route. They asked us to prevent any deletion until that lands.

tina_sre: I'm looking at delete-worker logs for object obj_0a1b2c3d. I see repeated failures around 2025-09-10T18:12:01Z: 
```
ERROR delete-worker: failed to decrypt envelope: KMS.Decrypt error: Key not found (keyId=projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/ring-1/cryptoKeys/rdw-acme-001)
```
Also a queued retry spike. Could be the customer KMS key was rotated/disabled. If we can't decrypt, deletion pipeline stalls and throws 500.

jake_eng: That fits. If the object was encrypted with a customer-managed key that is unavailable, our worker fails. Two paths: 1) Get KMS key restored/unlocked by customer — then re-run deletion. 2) If they want to halt deletion, we can set a retention hold record in our system (internal API) to prevent garbage collector from picking it up. Samir — does putting an internal hold require customer auth?

samir_security: Holds that affect retention are considered data custody actions. We need an explicit hold request from the customer. However, we can prepare a temporary safety measure: mark objects as 'hold_pending_verification' in a non-destructive flag visible to SRE/Support for 24h while we await docs. Need approval from legal/ops to extend.

maria_support: Customer asked for immediate logs export and KMS state verification. They also want timeline: if KMS not restored, when would GC remove the objects?

tina_sre: Current GC schedule: objects past TTL are eligible for deletion. For this account default 90d unless policy overrides. The job runs hourly; there is a configurable grace window of 72h for failed deletes. But if the delete pipeline errors permanently (e.g., decryption failure), items will remain in retry state for up to 7 days before escalation. In this case, because 500s are happening, GC will keep retrying — so not immediate irrevocable deletion today.

jake_eng: Action items I can do right now: 1) run targeted audit log export for object_id and retention_policy_id (will include KMS key id, timestamps, admin actions). 2) If customer provides KMS admin access or key restore, we can attempt decrypt flow test.

sre-bot: [alert] export-job-442 queued by jake_eng for customer acme-inc. ETA 15m.

samir_security: I'll draft the wording for the legal hold request we need them to sign (short form: confirm acct, object ids, scope, duration, contact). Maria — can you ask customer to attach that to the existing email thread and confirm expected SLA for our export?

maria_support: On it. I also asked if ACME can temporarily re-enable the KMS key or add our service account to decrypt so we can verify. They said they're checking with their security team.

tina_sre: Meanwhile I'll add a non-destructive 'hold_pending_verification' flag for obj_0a1b2c3d and rp_365_acme in our internal queue for 48h. This will not stop legal-required deletion later but will prevent GC from marking it final while we triage. Note: need approval from ops-lead to keep >24h.

jake_eng: Log export will include these fields: event_ts, actor, action (policy_update/delete/request), retention_policy_id, kms_key_id, object_id, operation_trace_id. Will post in thread when ready.

maria_support: Customer replied: "we can re-enable the key within 2 hours but need confirmation you'll not proceed with deletion until then". They will attach signed hold if needed.

samir_security: OK. We can accept a combination: their email + signed hold. For immediate safety, Tina's internal flag is fine for 48h. If legal hold not received within that window, escalate to SOC for decision.

tina_sre: Done — internal flag set, I annotated the GC dashboard.

jake_eng: Export ready: https://internal.redwood/export/442 — contains audit lines showing key change on 2025-08-30 and delete attempts 2025-09-10 18:12:01Z -> operation_trace_id=op_9f8e7d. KMS key id matches error. Sharing to secure-share with ACME contact.

maria_support: Sent to customer with note asking for signed hold if they want >48h. They confirmed they will re-enable key in ~90 minutes.

samir_security: Great. Keep this thread updated. After verify-decrypt we should run a dry-run deletion in staging for same object (no permanent action) to ensure pipeline healthy. Jake/Tina to coordinate.

jake_eng: I'll schedule the dry-run once ACME confirms key re-enabled.

maria_support: Closing loop — customer confirmed key re-enabled at 2025-09-10T20:05:00Z and we were able to decrypt and mark deletion complete in staging dry-run. They will send signed hold only if needed. ACME appreciates quick turn. :thumbsup:

tina_sre: Follow-up: I'll monitor GC for 72h and remove internal flag once stable.

samir_security: Filing a short post-incident note to compliance archive with audit export and timeline.

maria_support: Thanks team — resolving on our side. Will reopen if customer requests retention extension or legal hold.
